policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'dead through your trespasses and sins' has an unitalicized 'your', which renders ὑμῶν; the RP omission would leave no possessive to render.
ἤμεθα and ἦμεν are alternative imperfect forms of the same verb and person; ASV 'were' renders either.
The readings differ only in the gender and declension of πλοῦτος and its article and participle; ASV 'the exceeding riches' is identical either way.
ASV 'through faith' is anarthrous, but English regularly drops the article before an abstract noun, so it does not show whether RP's τῆς stood in the source.
The readings differ only in the order of ποτὲ and ὑμεῖς. ASV 'that once ye, the Gentiles' does not track Greek adverb position: at 2:2 it renders the pre-verbal ποτε as 'ye once walked'.
ASV 'ye were at that time' supplies 'at' for the dative of time whether or not RP's ἐν is present.
The readings differ only in the order of ἐγενήθητε and ἐγγὺς; English 'are made nigh' requires the verb before the adverb either way.
ASV 'that he might create in himself' is reflexive, which excludes the plain αὐτῷ of r01, but αὑτῷ and ἑαυτῷ are the contracted and uncontracted reflexive and render alike.
ASV 'preached peace to you that were far off, and peace to them that were nigh' repeats 'peace' without italics, rendering the second εἰρήνην that RP omits.
ASV 'but ye are fellow-citizens with the saints' repeats 'ye are' without italics, rendering the second ἐστὲ that RP omits.
ASV 'Christ Jesus himself being the chief corner stone' keeps the Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ order; the RP order would read 'Jesus Christ'.
ASV 'each several building' with the note 'Greek every building' renders an anarthrous πᾶσα οἰκοδομή; the added article of r01 would give 'the whole building'.
